theory.intro: Add or subtract the ordinates at the same input.
facts: Use only inputs where both functions are defined.
A table of corresponding ordinates helps build the combined graph.
Subtracting $g$ means adding $-g$; watch the signs.
Check intercepts, symmetry and asymptotic behaviour on the combined graph.

workedExamples.question_text: Sketch $f(x)=x^2-4$ and $g(x)=2x+1$ on the same axes. Then sketch $s(x)=f(x)+g(x)$ by adding corresponding ordinates.
Sketch $f(x)=x^2-2$ and $g(x)=2x+1$ on the same axes. Then sketch $d(x)=f(x)-g(x)$ by subtracting corresponding ordinates.
Sketch $y=x+\dfrac{9}{x}$ by adding corresponding ordinates. State its domain and describe its asymptotes.
For $f(x)=|x|$ and $g(x)=3$, sketch $y=f(x)-g(x)$ by subtracting corresponding ordinates.
Let $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=3$. Sketch their sum by adding corresponding ordinates.

foundation.question_text: Sketch the sum of $f(x)=x+1$ and $g(x)=1-x$ by adding corresponding ordinates.
Sketch the sum of $f(x)=x+1$ and $g(x)=2-x$ by adding corresponding ordinates.
Sketch the difference $f(x)-g(x)$ for $f(x)=x+1$ and $g(x)=3-x$ by subtracting corresponding ordinates.
Sketch the difference $f(x)-g(x)$ for $f(x)=x+1$ and $g(x)=4-x$ by subtracting corresponding ordinates.

development.question_text: Sketch the sum of $f(x)=x^2-2$ and $g(x)=x+1$ by adding corresponding ordinates.
Sketch the difference $f(x)-g(x)$ for $f(x)=x^2-3$ and $g(x)=x+1$ by subtracting corresponding ordinates.
